newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares extend losing streak to 5 days.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares extend losing streak to 5 days.

text.p: Slovenian shares closed 1.21 percent lower on meagre turnover on Thursday, extending their losses over five trading days.
Traders hold out little hope that the downward trek will soon end and see further losses over the medium term due to a dearth of active investors.
Traders said it was hard to determine at what levels prices would bottom-out due to widespread pessimism on the market -- generated by a clampdown on foreign trading activity last month.

But despite market sentiment festering at a low ebb, traders said good value could be picked up at relatively cheap prices in companies such food producers Droga and Kolinska, drug makers Lek and Krka and bank SKB.
The SBI index fell 1.21 percent or 16.21 points to 1,318.15. In last five consecutive days of falling the index fell 5.6 percent.

Last month the central bank ordered international investors to open custody accounts at Slovenian banks in order to be able to trade in Slovenian securities. Since then the SBI index has fallen 20.4 percent.

"It seems like our authorities are doing everything they can to force foreign investors out of the country, but I expect that will have to change as soon as this year due to Slovenia's bid for full membership in the European Union," Karmen Cerar, a trader at brokerage Poteza said.
Overall 10 shares fell, three rose and one was unchanged, while 11 were untraded. Turnover slumped to 46.9 million tolars from 83.2 million.
Bank SKB was the most active share, firming 1.35 percent to 52,700 tolars on volume of 255 shares for total turnover of 13.4 million tolars.
Brokerage Finmedia was the leading decliner, falling 7.69 percent to 12,000 tolars on volume of 86 shares.
Construction company GPG was the biggest gainer, jumping 7.58 percent to 7,100 tolars on volume of five shares.
